headline: Director Danny Boyle said he used AI to put Margaret Thatcher's face on an actor in his film Ink and did not ask her estate for permission.
score_reason: Kept at 5: the director's own account of a consent question in film, with no reaction from the estate or a legal test.
importance_line: Performers, estates and audiences are affected by how real people's faces are recreated with AI, but no complaint or ruling is reported.
summary: The Hollywood Reporter reports that director Danny Boyle said at the BFI London Film Festival that his film Ink, about Rupert Murdoch's rise, used AI to place Margaret Thatcher's face onto an impersonator, and that he chose not to ask her estate for permission. He said AI was used “very sparingly” and not to replace anyone.
notes: Full THR text read. Quote 'very sparingly' is Boyle's, from the interview as reported.
